official.status_note: The page describes standing schemes (national study grant, family allowance, faculty-allocated merit-based scholarships) without publishing a central call window.

Research scholarships available for academic projects (national and international calls)

Advice from the Welfare Office (Sozialreferat) of the students' union
eligibility: Austrian citizens, EEA citizens, stateless persons and refugees (as defined in Section 4 of the Student Support Act, StudFG)

requirements: Application per the requirements specified by the relevant faculty
selection_criteria: Outstanding academic results in accordance with the degree programme regulations
coverage: Merit-based scholarships for outstanding academic achievements
Research scholarships for academic projects, with calls published by the university
application_method: Apply to the relevant faculty, whose webpages carry further details of merit-based scholarships
official.application_route: Merit-based scholarship applications go through the relevant faculty; needs-based support runs through the national study grant
official.citizenship_residency: Austrian citizens, EEA citizens, stateless persons and refugees as defined in Section 4 StudFG
official.international_eligibility: Yes for EEA citizens and stateless persons or refugees with equal status; nationals of non-EEA countries are not covered by the merit-based scheme
official.description: The University of Graz points students to national support schemes such as the study grant and family allowance, and offers faculty-allocated merit-based scholarships for outstanding academic results, with eligibility limited to Austrian citizens, EEA citizens, stateless persons and refugees as defined in the Student Support Act.
official.program_type: University funding hub: faculty merit-based scholarships plus national support schemes

not_confirmed: funding_amount - no figure is published on the page
deadline_date - scholarship deadlines sit with each faculty
documents - no document list is published on the page
verification.notes: The official financing page confirms the merit-based scholarship eligibility groups (Austrian, EEA, stateless, refugee per Section 4 StudFG), the faculty-level application route, the tuition rates (EUR 25.20 per semester for the minimum duration plus tolerance semester, then EUR 363.36) and the signposting to stipendium.at, grants.at and the students' union Welfare Office. No amounts for the merit scholarships themselves are published.

applicant_utility.summary: Graz's own merit scholarships are allocated faculty by faculty, so the dean's office - not a central portal - decides; they are open to Austrian citizens, EEA citizens, stateless persons and refugees with outstanding grades. EU/EEA students with low family income should use the national study grant (stipendium.at) in parallel, and the students' union Welfare Office offers help with financial questions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: EEA and Austrian nationals enrolled in an ordinary Graz degree with outstanding results who can navigate their faculty's own scholarship rules.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your faculty's merit-scholarship rules - the university page deliberately points there
Confirm you fall within the eligible groups (Austrian, EEA, stateless persons, refugees per Section 4 StudFG)
If non-Austrian with low family income, apply for the national study grant via stipendium.at
Contact the Sozialreferat of the students' union for funding questions
common_rejection_risks: Applying centrally when decisions sit with the faculty
Being outside the eligible citizenship groups for the merit scholarship
Ignoring the national study grant, which is the larger funding route
Missing faculty-specific windows that the central page does not publish
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Graz; tuition is EUR 363.36 after the minimum duration plus tolerance semester (EUR 25.20 per semester during it).
document_audit: No central document list exists - each faculty sets its own evidence requirements
Outstanding results must be documented in line with the degree programme regulations
alerts: The reduced tuition rate is tied to the minimum study duration plus tolerance semester - extending your degree ends the EUR 25.20 rate
Family allowance is only available if parents live in Austria and stops at age 24
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Check faculty rules -> apply to the faculty -> separate application to stipendium.at for needs-based support.
